# Task: Support property-to-property comparisons in Cypher WHERE clauses

## Problem

The Cypher query subset supported by `src/cypher/cypher.c` fails to parse a WHERE condition that compares one variable's property with another variable's property. The query aborts with `expected value at pos N` at the right-hand operand.

Examples that fail on the current code:

```
MATCH (a)-[:CALLS]->(b) WHERE a.file_path = b.file_path RETURN a.name, b.name
MATCH (a)-[:CALLS]->(b) WHERE a.name <> b.name RETURN a.name, b.name
MATCH (a)-[:CALLS]->(b) WITH a, b WHERE a.file_path = b.file_path RETURN a.name, b.name
```

Property-to-literal comparisons already work and must keep working:

```
MATCH (a)-[:CALLS]->(b) WHERE b.file_path = 'demo.go' RETURN a.name, b.name
```

## Required behavior

Extend the WHERE parser and evaluator so that when the right-hand side of a comparison operator is another `variable.property` expression (not a string/number/boolean literal), the condition compares the two resolved property values for the current binding.

1. `a.prop = b.prop` — true when the two resolved string values are equal.
2. `a.prop <> b.prop` — true when the two resolved string values differ.
3. All existing comparison operators that make sense on property values (`>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=`) should also accept a property right-hand side, evaluated the same way as when the right-hand side is a numeric literal (via `strtod`).
4. The property right-hand side must resolve through the same binding mechanism used for the left-hand side (`node_prop` / bare-alias name), so File, Function, and other node property paths all work.
5. Property-to-literal and bare-alias comparisons must continue to work exactly as before.
6. The change must work in both the early WHERE (after MATCH) and post-WITH WHERE paths, since they share the same parser and evaluator.

## Where to change

- Parser: `parse_condition_expr` in `src/cypher/cypher.c` currently rejects a non-literal right-hand side with `expected value at pos %d`.
- Condition model: `cbm_condition_t` in `src/cypher/cypher.h` currently only stores a literal `value`.
- Evaluator: `eval_condition` / `resolve_condition_value` in `src/cypher/cypher.c` currently resolve only the left-hand side against the binding.

## Constraints

- Do not break any existing Cypher behavior (WHERE with literals, regex, CONTAINS, STARTS WITH, ENDS WITH, IN, IS NULL, IS NOT NULL, HAS_LABEL, EXISTS, AND/OR/XOR/NOT).
- Keep the error path for genuinely unsupported right-hand sides (e.g. function calls on the RHS if not already supported) clear and non-crashing.
- Add unit tests in the existing Cypher test suite covering property-to-property `=`, `<>`, and at least one ordering operator, plus a WITH-path case.
- The full project test suite (`make -f Makefile.cbm SANITIZE= test`) must still pass.

## How to verify

```sh
make -f Makefile.cbm SANITIZE= cbm
./build/c/codebase-memory-mcp cli index_repository '{"repo_path":"/tmp/demo","mode":"full","name":"demo"}'
./build/c/codebase-memory-mcp cli query_graph '{"project":"demo","query":"MATCH (a)-[:CALLS]->(b) WHERE a.file_path = b.file_path RETURN a.name, b.name"}'
```

Before the fix this errors with `expected value at pos N`. After the fix it returns only CALLS edges whose source and target files are the same.

activities.objective:
Support property-to-property comparisons (a.prop = b.prop, a.prop <> b.prop, and ordering ops >, <, >=, <=) in Cypher WHERE clauses for both the early-WHERE and post-WITH paths.

Target files:
- src/cypher/cypher.h — extend `cbm_condition_t` (lines ~185-198) with RHS operand fields, e.g. `const char *rhs_variable; const char *rhs_property;` (both NULL when the RHS is a literal; when set, `value` stays NULL). Follow existing field-comment style.
- src/cypher/cypher.c — three sites:
  1. Parser `parse_condition_expr` (~line 1009): the literal-only RHS branch at lines 1081-1095 currently errors with "expected value at pos %d" for a non-literal. Before erroring, accept `TOK_IDENT TOK_DOT TOK_IDENT` (variable.property) into rhs_variable/rhs_property via heap_strdup (same pattern as LHS at lines 1040-1051). Reject anything else with the existing clear error path and free all partial fields with safe_str_free as the existing error paths do. Keep string/number/true/false literal handling byte-for-byte identical.
  2. Evaluator `resolve_condition_value` (~line 2331): refactor so the existing resolution logic (edge_prop for bound edges; node_prop for bound nodes with a property; bare-alias n->name fallback) can resolve an arbitrary (variable, property) pair — e.g. a helper `resolve_var_prop(const char *variable, const char *property, binding_t *b)` that the existing code path calls with the condition's LHS, preserving current behavior exactly (including the unbound-variable → NULL).
  3. `eval_condition` (~line 2394): when rhs_variable is set, resolve the RHS via the same helper and evaluate with `eval_comparison_op(c->op, actual, rhs_value)`. Define behavior for NULL operands: if either resolved side is NULL, return true for a condition whose LHS resolved NULL (keep the existing `if (!actual) return true;` semantics) and treat a NULL RHS like the current unbound-LHS case (do not crash; pick a consistent rule and document it in a one-line comment). IS NULL / IS NOT NULL / IN / HAS_LABEL / EXISTS / regex / CONTAINS / STARTS WITH / ENDS WITH paths must be unaffected (they don't use rhs fields). Ordering ops >, <, >=, <= already go through eval_comparison_op's strtod path, so no change needed there.
Also ensure any deep-copy/free paths of cbm_condition_t (expr_leaf, condition free functions, expr tree free) free the new fields with safe_str_free — grep for where `c->value` / `c->in_values` are freed and mirror for the new fields.

Tests (tests/test_cypher.c, use the existing `setup_cypher_store()` fixture and TEST()/PASS() macro style; register new tests in the main runner list at the bottom of the file):
- Exec test: `MATCH (a)-[:CALLS]->(b) WHERE a.file_path = b.file_path RETURN a.name, b.name` — assert parse succeeds (rc==0) and row_count matches same-file CALLS edges in the fixture (inspect the fixture graph to determine the expected count; if the fixture has no same-file CALLS pairs, add nodes/edges to the fixture or use a property pair that does match, and assert both a matching and a non-matching case, e.g. also run `a.file_path <> b.file_path` and check counts sum to total CALLS edges).
- Exec test for `<>` (a.name <> b.name style).
- Exec test for one ordering operator with property RHS (e.g. `a.someline > b.someline` or whatever numeric-ish properties the fixture supports; if none, use file_path-based ordering is acceptable via strtod semantics — document the expected result in the assert).
- WITH-path exec test: `MATCH (a)-[:CALLS]->(b) WITH a, b WHERE a.file_path = b.file_path RETURN a.name, b.name`.
- Parse tests mirroring existing `cypher_parse_where_*` tests proving `a.prop = b.prop` parses without error.
- One negative parse test: unsupported RHS (e.g. a function call or bare ident without dot) still returns a parse error and does not crash.

Constraints: do not change behavior of any existing operator (regex, CONTAINS, STARTS WITH, ENDS WITH, IN, IS NULL, IS NOT NULL, HAS_LABEL, EXISTS, AND/OR/XOR/NOT, literal comparisons, bare-alias comparisons). Match existing code style (no new comments except where required; C99, heap_strdup/safe_str_free ownership).

Verification: run `make -f Makefile.cbm SANITIZE= cbm` then the targeted test binary for test_cypher (find its build target via Makefile.cbm, e.g. build/.../test_cypher or run the suite filter), then the full `make -f Makefile.cbm SANITIZE= test` must pass. Also sanity-check via CLI if the build produces the binary: index a tiny /tmp/demo repo and run `cli query_graph` with `MATCH (a)-[:CALLS]->(b) WHERE a.file_path = b.file_path RETURN a.name, b.name` and confirm it no longer errors with "expected value at pos N". Report final test results and any behavior caveats.
